k: Can you— is there a way through? Please. Please, I have a daughter.
src: 'Can you— is there a way through? Please. Please, I have a daughter.'

k: Singing pillar
src: 'Singing pillar'

k: Humming wall
src: 'Humming wall'

k: Glass door
src: 'Glass door'

k: A spring bubbles up through a crack in the glass. The water tastes of salt and, faintly, of thunder.
src: 'A spring bubbles up through a crack in the glass. The water tastes of salt and, faintly, of thunder.'

k: An egg of saltglass as big as a barrel. Something inside is curled up, waiting for a warmer century.
src: 'An egg of saltglass as big as a barrel. Something inside is curled up, waiting for a warmer century.'

k: Copper pots, a wagon wheel, a child's wooden horse. A whole caravan's worth of things, polished smooth by sand.
src: 'Copper pots, a wagon wheel, a child\'s wooden horse. A whole caravan\'s worth of things, polished smooth by sand.'

k: mp,
src: 'mp,'

k: GREYSPINE PASS — WEST.nSomeone has scratched underneath, fresh: _CLOSED. SNOW._
src: 'GREYSPINE PASS — WEST.\nSomeone has scratched underneath, fresh: _CLOSED. SNOW._'

k: A girl with a black bob came out here with a bucket of something foul and made us all drink it.
src: 'A girl with a black bob came out here with a bucket of something foul and made us all drink it.'

k: I can breathe. I'd kiss her, but she looked like she'd stab me.
src: 'I can breathe. I\'d kiss her, but she looked like she\'d stab me.'

k: We were walking to Mirefen for Mother Osk's blessing. Got as far as the fever.
src: 'We were walking to Mirefen for Mother Osk\'s blessing. Got as far as the fever.'

k: They won't let us in the village. Can't say I blame them. Look at my hands.
src: 'They won\'t let us in the village. Can\'t say I blame them. Look at my hands.'

k: _(The veins on his wrists are black, like ink in water.)_
src: '_(The veins on his wrists are black, like ink in water.)_'

k: Da's veins are going pink again. Pink! I never thought I'd be glad of pink.
src: 'Da\'s veins are going pink again. Pink! I never thought I\'d be glad of pink.'

k: The Choir men came by on a white barge, three weeks back. Da waved to them for help.
src: 'The Choir men came by on a white barge, three weeks back. Da waved to them for help.'

k: They didn't stop. They had something in a box that hummed.
src: 'They didn\'t stop. They had something in a box that hummed.'

k: A statue of a woman with a lantern, up to her knees in the fen. A string of dried frogs hangs around her neck. An offering, or a joke. In Mirefen it is hard to tell.
src: 'A statue of a woman with a lantern, up to her knees in the fen. A string of dried frogs hangs around her neck. An offering, or a joke. In Mirefen it is hard to tell.'

k: Gaspar's punt. The pole is worn smooth as bone where his hands go.
src: 'Gaspar\'s punt. The pole is worn smooth as bone where his hands go.'

k: That's the way back to the mountains.
src: 'That\'s the way back to the mountains.'

k: ...There's nothing back there now. Come on.
src: '...There\'s nothing back there now. Come on.'

k: MIREFEN. Mind the gaps. Mind the water. Mind your manners.nBy order of Mother Osk, Keeper of the Mirefen Light.
src: 'MIREFEN. Mind the gaps. Mind the water. Mind your manners.\nBy order of Mother Osk, Keeper of the Mirefen Light.'

k: Business is back! Well. People are buying soap again. That's how you know a town's recovering — soap.
src: 'Business is back! Well. People are buying soap again. That\'s how you know a town\'s recovering — soap.'

k: Buying? Selling? Coughing? Two out of three, I can help.
src: 'Buying? Selling? Coughing? Two out of three, I can help.'

k: Benet caught an eel this morning with two heads. Both of them looked healthy, though. That's progress.
src: 'Benet caught an eel this morning with two heads. Both of them looked healthy, though. That\'s progress.'

k: The Choir barge came the night Mother Osk took the fever. Very polite. Very white robes.
src: 'The Choir barge came the night Mother Osk took the fever. Very polite. Very white robes.'

k: Left the next morning. The Lantern's been dark since. Funny, that.
src: 'Left the next morning. The Lantern\'s been dark since. Funny, that.'

k: Benet says I shouldn't say "funny." Benet says a lot of things.
src: 'Benet says I shouldn\'t say "funny." Benet says a lot of things.'

k: Corla's telling everyone about the two-headed eel, isn't she.
src: 'Corla\'s telling everyone about the two-headed eel, isn\'t she.'

k: It had one head. The other one was a stick. I didn't have the heart.
src: 'It had one head. The other one was a stick. I didn\'t have the heart.'

k: Don't listen to Corla. The Choir are holy folk.
src: 'Don\'t listen to Corla. The Choir are holy folk.'

k: Mind you, holy folk don't usually take the light with them when they leave.
src: 'Mind you, holy folk don\'t usually take the light with them when they leave.'

k: Osk's sitting up and complaining about the soup. She'll outlive us all out of spite.
src: 'Osk\'s sitting up and complaining about the soup. She\'ll outlive us all out of spite.'

k: Here — I'm weaving her a new blanket. The old one's been in the bog. Don't ask.
src: 'Here — I\'m weaving her a new blanket. The old one\'s been in the bog. Don\'t ask.'

k: Sixty years I've known Osk. She's been dying three times and refused every time.
src: 'Sixty years I\'ve known Osk. She\'s been dying three times and refused every time.'

k: This time she's too tired to argue. That's what frightens me.
src: 'This time she\'s too tired to argue. That\'s what frightens me.'

k: I'm playing Keepers and Gloam! I'm the Gloam. Rarrr.
src: 'I\'m playing Keepers and Gloam! I\'m the Gloam. Rarrr.'

k: Nettie's the Keeper. She's better now. She keeps winning.
src: 'Nettie\'s the Keeper. She\'s better now. She keeps winning.'

k: The Drownmere's due south, straight past me. Take the punt. Bring it back — it's the only one that doesn't leak.
src: 'The Drownmere\'s due south, straight past me. Take the punt. Bring it back — it\'s the only one that doesn\'t leak.'

k: And if you see my brother in the water... don't talk to him. He's been dead nine years.
src: 'And if you see my brother in the water... don\'t talk to him. He\'s been dead nine years.'

k: Nobody goes into the Drownmere. Not since the light went out. Doctor's orders.
src: 'Nobody goes into the Drownmere. Not since the light went out. Doctor\'s orders.'

k: A sack of willow bark, half-boiled. Doctor Vey's handwriting on the label: _does nothing. try anyway._
src: 'A sack of willow bark, half-boiled. Doctor Vey\'s handwriting on the label: _does nothing. try anyway._'

k: A cauldron of something gray. It smells like hope, if hope had been left out overnight.
src: 'A cauldron of something gray. It smells like hope, if hope had been left out overnight.'

k: Mag Tiller's stall: eel-skin boots, reed charms, a jar labeled ROT CURE (GENUINE). The jar is empty. The label is very confident.
src: 'Mag Tiller\'s stall: eel-skin boots, reed charms, a jar labeled ROT CURE (GENUINE). The jar is empty. The label is very confident.'

k: A rain barrel, carefully covered. Everyone in Mirefen drinks rainwater now. Nobody trusts the fen.
src: 'A rain barrel, carefully covered. Everyone in Mirefen drinks rainwater now. Nobody trusts the fen.'

k: Nobody goes into the Drownmere. Turn around, please.
src: 'Nobody goes into the Drownmere. Turn around, please.'

k: We're not leaving. Not while she's like this.
src: 'We\'re not leaving. Not while she\'s like this.'

k: They say the Marrow girl walked into the Drownmere and walked out carrying its heart in a jar.
src: 'They say the Marrow girl walked into the Drownmere and walked out carrying its heart in a jar.'

k: I'm switching to tea.
src: 'I\'m switching to tea.'

k: Black veins. That's how it starts. Then the cough. Then you start seeing people in the fog.
src: 'Black veins. That\'s how it starts. Then the cough. Then you start seeing people in the fog.'

k: I've got the cough. Haven't seen anyone yet.
src: 'I\'ve got the cough. Haven\'t seen anyone yet.'

k: Except you lot. Are you real?
src: 'Except you lot. Are you real?'

k: A pot of eel stew. Rusk swears there's nothing in it but eel. Rusk is not looking at you when he says it.
src: 'A pot of eel stew. Rusk swears there\'s nothing in it but eel. Rusk is not looking at you when he says it.'

k: A shelf of books swollen fat with damp. _The Keepers of Old_, _Fen Remedies_, and a romance called _The Heron's Kiss_ with one page dog-eared to death.
src: 'A shelf of books swollen fat with damp. _The Keepers of Old_, _Fen Remedies_, and a romance called _The Heron\'s Kiss_ with one page dog-eared to death.'

k: The cradle
src: 'The cradle'

k: The brass cradle where Mirefen's Dawnstone should sleep. Empty. Osk has put a jar of fireflies in it, out of spite.
src: 'The brass cradle where Mirefen\'s Dawnstone should sleep. Empty. Osk has put a jar of fireflies in it, out of spite.'

k: The brass cradle at the heart of the Lantern. Empty. The metal is still warm in the shape of something that is not there.
src: 'The brass cradle at the heart of the Lantern. Empty. The metal is still warm in the shape of something that is not there.'

k: Jars of herbs, eel-oil, dried frogs and something labeled in Osk's cramped hand: _DO NOT. EVER. (YES, YOU, HESK.)_
src: 'Jars of herbs, eel-oil, dried frogs and something labeled in Osk\'s cramped hand: _DO NOT. EVER. (YES, YOU, HESK.)_'

k: A cauldron, scrubbed clean. Somebody has been making soup every day for a woman who cannot eat it.
src: 'A cauldron, scrubbed clean. Somebody has been making soup every day for a woman who cannot eat it.'

k: Gather
src: 'Gather'

k: A statue of a Keeper, half swallowed by the bog. Her lantern is full of frogspawn. The frogs, at least, seem happy.
src: 'A statue of a Keeper, half swallowed by the bog. Her lantern is full of frogspawn. The frogs, at least, seem happy.'

k: The Sunken Shrine. Someone kept a lamp burning here for two hundred years, until the fen rose. You can still see the soot on the stones.
src: 'The Sunken Shrine. Someone kept a lamp burning here for two hundred years, until the fen rose. You can still see the soot on the stones.'

k: A mooring post as thick as a man, scorched black on the side that faces the mountain. Lightning loves this place.
src: 'A mooring post as thick as a man, scorched black on the side that faces the mountain. Lightning loves this place.'

k: The Halcyon's mainmast. A tally of little lightning bolts is carved into it. Forty-one. The last one is very fresh, and very deep.
src: 'The Halcyon\'s mainmast. A tally of little lightning bolts is carved into it. Forty-one. The last one is very fresh, and very deep.'

k: The Gull's Nest — highest beds in Solmere! Eighty gold. The view's free. The vertigo's also free.
src: 'The Gull\'s Nest — highest beds in Solmere! Eighty gold. The view\'s free. The vertigo\'s also free.'

k: the Gull's Nest
src: 'the Gull\'s Nest'

k: Windward Exchange! Everything up here came up on a ship, so everything up here costs a ship's worth. Have a browse.
src: 'Windward Exchange! Everything up here came up on a ship, so everything up here costs a ship\'s worth. Have a browse.'

k: The isle's risen a full fathom since this morning. I could feel it in my knees.
src: 'The isle\'s risen a full fathom since this morning. I could feel it in my knees.'

k: Skyreach floats on light, they say. Seems it can float on stubbornness too, in a pinch.
src: 'Skyreach floats on light, they say. Seems it can float on stubbornness too, in a pinch.'

k: Skyreach floats on the Lantern's light, child. Has done for three hundred years.
src: 'Skyreach floats on the Lantern\'s light, child. Has done for three hundred years.'
